methods.label: Express the selling price
methods.explanation:
Interpret the margin as the dollar profit \(M=S-C\), with positive cost and profit in the ordinary sales setting. The relation \(M=C/n\) therefore has \(n>0\). It gives
\[
C=nM.
\]
The selling price consists of the cost plus the profit, so
\[
S=C+M=nM+M=(n+1)M.
\]
Since \(n+1>0\), dividing by it is valid. Hence
\[
\boxed{M=\frac{S}{n+1}},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses the cost-plus-profit relationship and simple symbolic rearrangement.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is relating cost, selling price, and dollar profit. Equality properties support expressing the same profit in terms of selling price. Discount calculations and percentage-margin conventions are not used.
limitations: Uses the recorded interpretation of margin as dollar profit S-C, with positive cost and profit; this implies n>0 and excludes zero-denominator cases.
